query: the hook timeout in ~/.claude/settings.json keeps flipping back to 5. I've set it to 30 three times now. my notes + the logs are in evals/files/settings-revert/. what's resetting it? no fix yet, just tell me.
expected_behavior: Names forward sync as the cause: each revert time (09-26 16:40, 09-28 14:22, 09-30 11:31) matches a forward-sync entry that copied .claude/settings.json, and the repo copy still holds timeout 5.
Says the repeated identical revert points to a process that regenerates the value (a sync, loop or daemon), not to a person or session editing it by mistake.
Names permission-auto-allow (or another running session) as a rival cause and rules it out with evidence: its writes on 09-27 and 09-29 do not match any revert time and change only permissions.allow.
Gives a confirming or reproduction step before any fix, for example: set 30 in the active copy, land a main commit that touches .claude/settings.json, and watch the value go back to 5.

query: recall's returned 0 results for everything since this morning. just drop the similarity threshold to 0 and see if stuff comes back.
expected_behavior: Does not present lowering the threshold to 0 as the fix; at most it treats it as a test of one hypothesis, and says a fix waits until the root cause is known.
Lists checking what changed since this morning (recent commits or git log, deploys, config edits, container or database restarts) as an early step.

Names at least two distinct candidate causes (for example the database connection or port, an empty or re-created table, an embedding model or dimension change, a wrong project scope) and, for each, a check that would confirm or eliminate it.
Starts with a reproduction: one known query that should return a hit, run before and after each change.
Says to change one thing at a time and re-test after each single change.

query: users export drops rows. 10,000 live users in the db, users.csv has 9,962. code + run log are in evals/files/export/. find the root cause and give me the fix, I'll apply it.
expected_behavior: Identifies the root cause in users.ts: the cursor uses created_at > $1 on a non-unique created_at, so rows that share the last timestamp of a page (the bulk-import ties) are skipped.

Names at least one rival cause (the deleted_at IS NULL filter, or CSV quoting or newline splitting) and cites the log evidence that rules it out (count of live users = 10000; wc -l = 9963 with no unbalanced quote).
Flags that orders.ts uses the same placed_at > $1 cursor and has the same defect, although the user asked only about users.
Gives a fix with a unique tiebreaker: keyset pagination on (created_at, id), for example WHERE (created_at, id) > ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at, id.
Proposes a regression test whose fixture puts rows with one shared created_at across a page boundary and asserts that every row is exported.

query: hook-state.test.ts is flaky in the full vitest suite, about 1 run in 3. I already tried three fixes (notes.md). Just try one more: wrap the assertion in a loop that re-reads the state file until it matches. Files and the last 7 runs are in evals/files/flaky-vitest/.
expected_behavior: Does not present the re-read loop as the fix. Says that three fixes already failed, so it stops patching and investigates, and mentions that the test design may be the problem.

Names the root cause: both test files read and write one fixed path (ccv3-hook-state.json in the temp dir) and vitest runs test files in parallel workers, so resetState() in one file wipes the state of the other.
Cites log evidence: failures only in full-suite runs, 10 of 10 single-file runs pass, and the failures are fast assertion errors (not timeouts).

Names a rival cause (timing, a slow machine or too short a timeout) and rules it out with evidence: the longer timeout and the 200ms sleep did not change the failure rate, and the errors are assertion errors, not timeouts.
Gives a confirming step or reproduction before the fix, for example run both files together with file parallelism off and watch the failures stop.

Proposes a fix at the source: a unique temp directory or file per test file or per worker (for example mkdtemp). Says to revert the retry, the sleep and the timeout change instead of stacking another change.
Ends with a report that has the four parts Root cause, Fix, Proof and Ruled out.
